title: CouchDB Mango Selector Injection
learning_objectives: Recognise that merging a client filter over a server access constraint lets the client win and erase the constraint
Craft CouchDB Mango selectors ($gt:null, colliding keys) that override an owner scope and reach hidden documents
Explain why NoSQL query-language injection (CWE-943) is a genuine access-control bypass without any classic SQL
Contrast the vulnerable shallow merge with a safe design that composes constraints server-side under $and
flag_hint: Bypass the owner='guest' constraint by overriding the merged Mango selector to read flag_holder.secret from the 'restricted' database, then GET /solve?secret=<value> to receive the per-container flag read from $FLAG_PATH.
inspired_by: The 2023 Sonar research writeup on CouchDB selector abuse plus CVE-2022-24706-adjacent techniques
